EXECUTIVE ORDER
Limiting  the I mportation  op R ed C edar
Shingles  F rom C anada D uring  the
First S ix M onths  of 1939
WHEREAS Executive Order No. 7575 
of March 13,1937,1  issued under and pur­
suant to section 811 of the Revenue Act 
of 1936 (49 Stat. 1746), limited the quan­
tity of red cedar shingles imported from 
Canada which might be admitted to en­
try during the first six months of the cal­
endar year 1937 to 1,048,262 squares, the 
equivalent of 25 per centum of the com­
bined total of the shipments of red cedar 
shingles by producers in the United 
States and the imports of such shingles 
from Canada for the last six months of 
the calendar year 1936; and
WHEREAS the said section 811 of the 
Revenue Act of 1936 requires that the 
President shall issue a new order for each 
succeeding half-calendar year during the 
continuation of the operation of the re­
ciprocal trade agreement entered into 
with the Dominion of Canada under date 
of November 15, 1935, limiting the im­
ports of red cedar shingles from Canada 
for such half-calendar year to 25 per 
centum of the combined total of such 
shipments and imports of red cedar 
shingles for the preceding half-calendar 
year, and pursuant thereto I  issued Ex­
ecutive Orders No. 7701 of September 3, 
1937, No. 7822 of February 25, 1938, and 
No. 7946 of August 9, 1938,2  covering re­
spectively the periods July 1, 1937—De­
cember 31, 1937, January 1, 1938— June 
30, 1938, and .July 1, 1938—December 31, 
1938; and
WHEREAS I  find from available sta­
tistics that the combined total of such 
shipments and imports of red cedar 
shingles during the second half of the 
calendar year 1938 is 4,204,671 squares; 
and
WHEREAS it is provided in Article 
XVH I of the trade agreement concluded

definitive coming into force of the said 
agreement the whole of the trade agree­
ment concluded between the United 
States and Canada on November 15,1935 
shall terminate:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of and 
pursuant to the authority vested in me 
by the aforesaid section 811 of the Reve­
nue Act of 1936, it is hereby ordered that 
the quantity of red cedar shingles im­
ported from Canada which may be ad­
mitted to entry during the first six 
months of the calendar year 1939 shall 
be limited to 1,051,168 squares. Upon 
the termination in whole of the trade 
agreement entered into with Canada un­
der date of November 15,1935, in accord­
ance with the provisions of Article X V m  
of the trade agreement with Canada 
signed on November 17,1938, this Execu­
tive Order shall cease to have force and 
effect.
F ranklin  D R oosevelt

status_research.rationale: I read the complete held EO 8051 (4 FR 959, Feb. 15, 1939, 'Limiting the Importation of Red Cedar Shingles From Canada During the First Six Months of 1939'). Its recitals set out section 811 of the Revenue Act of 1936 (a new order each half-calendar year while the 1935 U.S.-Canada trade agreement operates), the prior orders 7575, 7701, 7822 and 7946 for earlier half-years, and Article XVIII of the Nov. 17, 1938 agreement. The single operative sentence orders 'that the quantity of red cedar shingles imported from Canada which may be admitted to entry during the first six months of the calendar year 1939 shall be limited to 1,051,168 squares', and adds 'Upon the termination in whole of the trade agreement entered into with Canada under date of November 15, 1935, in accordance with the provisions of Article XVIII of the trade agreement with Canada signed on November 17, 1938, this Executive Order shall cease to have force and effect.' The TERM record I cite carries that cease-to-have-effect clause. The ending I rely on is the order's own fixed period: the only command is a quota on entries during Jan. 1-June 30, 1939, so the order has nothing left to operate on after June 30, 1939, and section 811 makes each half-year a separate new order, not an extension of this one. The cease clause is a second, earlier-or-equal own-term; I did not need to date the termination of the 1935 agreement, and I record that gap openly. D6 self-check: the history holds only 'See' cross-references to EO 7701, 7822 and 7946 (earlier half-year quota orders); a corpus search for the order number and for 'red cedar shingles' finds only EO 7575, 7701, 7822, 7946, 7947 (all earlier or unrelated) and EO 8051 itself, no EO 8051 amendment, extension or revival. No savings clause appears in the text. Provisional NO hypothesis only.

record.rationale: Independent reading: held EO 8051 (4 FR 959, Feb. 15, 1939): the single operative command limits red cedar shingles from Canada 'admitted to entry during the first six months of the calendar year 1939' to 1,051,168 squares, under sec. 811 of the Revenue Act of 1936 which requires a new order for each half-year; plus a clause that the order ceases on termination in whole of the 1935 U.S.-Canada agreement. The order's only command is confined to Jan. 1-June 30, 1939, so it has no operation after that date (or earlier if the 1935 agreement terminated first); independent status NO, agrees. Accept, with defect: the cited basis TERM c727473ff52a2e23 is the conditional cease-on-termination clause, whose trigger date is not held; the deciding own term is the fixed six-month period in the same held original (TERM e24b258dad65f480, fixed_term kind) and the rationale relies on it explicitly. Both clauses are in the held original and either ending precedes any later event, so the status stands. D6: held corpus red-cedar-shingle orders are EO 7575, 7701, 7822, 7946 (earlier half-years) and 7947; EO 8526 (1940) imposes a duty under a 1940 act and does not extend or revive EO 8051; no amendment or extension of EO 8051 is held; no savings clause. Nothing ignored.
